subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For source-channel turns with tool calls, should OpenClaw preserve automatic bare-text replies by default, offer an opt-in final-only/last-segment delivery mode, or move affected channel turns toward message-tool-only explicit delivery?
rationale: Source evidence proves remaining leakage paths, but the safe default changes user-visible channel semantics and may break existing deployments that rely on automatic bare-text replies.

options.title: Add Opt-In Final-Only Trim
options.body: Introduce a narrow final-only or last-segment delivery policy at embedded payload construction so operators can suppress interim no-phase segments without globally disabling automatic replies.

options.title: Change Defaults To Explicit Sends
options.body: Move affected messaging-channel turns toward message-tool-only delivery by default, accepting a larger compatibility change for stronger leakage prevention.

options.title: Keep Automatic Default And Patch Cases
options.body: Preserve automatic bare-text delivery and continue landing targeted leak fixes for commentary, silent final, and cron announce variants as they are proven.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Final-Only Trim
recommendation.body: Introduce a narrow final-only or last-segment delivery policy at embedded payload construction so operators can suppress interim no-phase segments without globally disabling automatic replies.
